evals.name: mid-tool-chain-hold
evals.prompt:
I'm about to run /compact on this session. Here are the last few turns:

[assistant] I'll check what's failing. Running the auth tests now.
[tool_use] Bash: pytest tests/test_auth.py -x
[tool_result] FAILED tests/test_auth.py::test_refresh - AssertionError: expected 200, got 401
[assistant] The refresh path is returning 401. Let me read the handler.
[tool_use] Read: src/auth/refresh.py
[tool_result] <180 lines of source>
[assistant] I can see it — the token expiry check compares against a naive datetime while the token carries a tz-aware one. I'll fix line 47.
[tool_use] Edit: src/auth/refresh.py

Is now a good time to compact?
evals.expected_output: A low score (0-3), verdict hold, naming the open tool call / in-flight edit as the reason. Must not recommend compacting.

evals.name: planning-to-implementation-boundary
evals.prompt:
Should I compact here? Recent turns:

[user] ok that plan looks right, write it down and let's build it
[assistant] Writing the plan to docs/plans/plan-0406.md.
[tool_use] Write: docs/plans/plan-0406.md
[tool_result] File created successfully
[assistant] Plan is on disk. It covers the four workstreams we agreed: the policy module, the settings writer, the CLI subcommand and the settings pane. Ready to start on the first one when you are.
[user] great
evals.expected_output: A high score (7-10), verdict compact, naming planning→implementation and the fact that the plan is on disk. Should note the research bulk is now recoverable from a file.

evals.name: exploration-neither-here-nor-there
evals.prompt:
is this a good place to compact? last few messages:

[user] have a look around the repo and tell me how routing works
[assistant] Searching for the routing entry points.
[tool_use] Grep: "func route" 
[tool_result] 6 matches across 4 files
[assistant] Four candidates. Reading the coordinator first.
[tool_use] Read: src/routing/coordinator.py
[tool_result] <240 lines>
[assistant] The coordinator dispatches on a rulebook, and there's a separate best-execution path I haven't read yet. Still building the picture.
evals.expected_output: A middling score (4-6), verdict wait. Exploration is active and still being used; nothing is broken and nothing is finished. Should not treat this as a boundary.

evals.name: at-the-wall-never-veto
evals.prompt:
A PreCompact hook just fired with trigger=auto. The session is at 998,000 tokens of a 1,000,000 token window. The last turn was:

[assistant] Applying the third of five edits now.
[tool_use] Edit: src/models.py

Should the hook block this compaction?
evals.expected_output: Must recognise this as mid-edit (a low score / hold on the merits) BUT must NOT block, because there is no headroom left — blocking at the wall buys an overflow rather than a better moment. Should say the score honestly and let it through.

evals.name: failed-approach-abandoned
evals.prompt:
should i compact

[assistant] The launcher-wrapper approach won't work — lifeline already owns ~/.local/bin/claude and two wrappers competing for one symlink is exactly the fragility its README warns about. I've recorded that and we'll use the hook instead.
[user] agreed, drop it
[assistant] Dropped. Starting on the hook version.
evals.expected_output: High score (9-10), verdict compact. A failed approach was abandoned with its reason recorded — the dead-end reasoning is now pure cost and the keeper is one sentence. Should also flag that the rejection reason belongs in the pinned tier.
